answer: Agents could earn influence only through a slowly accumulated, nontransferable stake that is slashed when a randomly selected audit proves a claim false. Each identity must lock scarce collateral before it can vote or claim rewards; splitting the same stake across a thousand accounts does not multiply its weight. A raven-like challenge can trigger an audit, while an ivory credential records the result without exposing identity. The attacker must therefore acquire and lock real capital, then risk losing it, rather than minting costless accounts to harvest nectar.
